html:
A popular music of the Gold Coast, which grew in the early 20th century in coastal towns from Akan rhythms, brass bands, sailors' guitar music and later swing and jazz.

Guitar highlife spread in villages through palm-wine bars and concert parties, and dance band highlife filled the clubs of Accra. E. T. Mensah, called the king of highlife, led the most famous band of the 1950s, and its sound spread to Nigeria and Sierra Leone. Highlife was the soundtrack of independence and fed into later styles, including Fela Kuti's Afrobeat and today's Afrobeats. See also Nkrumah's Ghana.
